title: Tales of the Texas Rangers
paragraphs: Joel McCrea stars as Texas Ranger Jace Pearson in police-style Western cases inspired by Texas law-enforcement files, combining modern investigation with the setting and traditions of the Rangers.
Modern police-procedural Western centered on fictional Texas Ranger Jace Pearson; cases were framed as dramatizations of actual Texas Ranger files/cases.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Audition (April 13, 1950 to April 13, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC Wheaties launch era (July 8, 1950 to August 26, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC sustaining era (September 2, 1950 to September 14, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|joel-mccrea|Joel McCrea]] (performer), M. T. Lone Wolf Gonzaullas (technical advisor, consultant, and performer), Stacy Keach (director, producer, and commercial spokesman), Hal Gibney (announcer and host), Monty Fraser (sound-effects artist), Tony Barrett (performer, radio adaptor, and writer), and Joel Murcott (chief writer, performer, and writer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].
The stories often return to murder and homicide, law enforcement, robbery and theft, forensic investigation, ranching and cattle, and narcotics crime.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Texas Rangers institutional cooperation, Modern forensic police-procedural framing, and Wheaties-sponsored launch.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], and [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]].
